_meta.note: verbatim fields contain exact captured output. commentary fields contain human interpretation.

wrapperFormat.verbatim: Tool results are returned in <result><name>{ToolName}</name><output>{content}</output></result> blocks. Errors use <result><name>{ToolName}</name><error>{message}</error></result>. Multiple parallel results are wrapped in <function_results>...</function_results>. A <system-reminder> block with token count follows each result batch.
wrapperFormat.commentary: The harness wraps each tool call result in XML result tags with name and output/error fields. Parallel calls produce multiple result blocks in a single function_results wrapper. Token budget reminders are injected as system-reminder tags after results.

full_file_success.verbatim:
1	Line 1: Greetings, Universe! ...
2	Line 2: ...
...
20	Line 20: Final line with trailing newline.
21
full_file_success.commentary: Output uses cat -n format: line_number TAB content. Line numbers start at 1. Empty lines show just the line number and tab. A trailing empty line (21) appears for files ending with a newline.

partial_with_offset_limit.verbatim:
5	Line 5: Special characters: ...
6	Line 6: Unicode: ...
7	Line 7: Blank line follows:
partial_with_offset_limit.commentary: Offset is 0-based line position (offset:5 starts at line 5). Limit restricts to N lines. Only the requested range is returned with original line numbers preserved.

file_not_found.verbatim: File does not exist. Note: your current working directory is C:\AI\MOSAIC\MOSAIC.
file_not_found.commentary: Error message includes the working directory for context. Returned in the <error> wrapper instead of <output>.

large_file_truncation.verbatim:
1	foxtrot golf [ROW:0001] hotel india
...
1518	foxtrot golf [ROW:1518] hotel india

<system-reminder>
[Truncated: PARTIAL view — ...large-file-3000-lines.txt: showing lines 1-1518 of 3001 total (42006 tokens, cap 25000). Call Read with offset=1519 limit=1518 for the next page, or Grep to find a specific section. Do NOT answer from this page alone if the answer may be further in the file.]
</system-reminder>
large_file_truncation.commentary: Despite documentation saying 2000-line default, actual truncation is TOKEN-based (cap 25000 tokens). For this file, 1518 lines fit within the token cap. The truncation message includes total lines, token count, token cap, and pagination instructions. Injected as a system-reminder block after the content.

new_file_success.call: Write({file_path: scratchpad/write-test.txt, content: 'Test file written by capture process.'})
new_file_success.verbatim: File created successfully at: C:\Users\tgurt\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\...\scratchpad\write-test.txt (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)
new_file_success.commentary: Success message includes full path and a hint not to re-read the file. Uses 'created' for new files.

success.call: Edit({file_path: edit-test-copy.txt, old_string: 'Line 16: Swap this line with different content.', new_string: 'Line 16: EDITED SUCCESSFULLY by capture test.'})
success.verbatim: The file C:\...\edit-test-copy.txt has been updated successfully. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)
success.commentary: Success message includes full path and the same no-re-read hint as Write. Uses 'updated' for edits.

string_not_found.call: Edit({file_path: edit-test-copy.txt, old_string: 'THIS STRING DOES NOT EXIST IN THE FILE', new_string: 'replacement'})
string_not_found.verbatim:
<tool_use_error>String to replace not found in file.
String: THIS STRING DOES NOT EXIST IN THE FILE</tool_use_error>
string_not_found.commentary: Error wrapped in <tool_use_error> tags (inside the <error> result wrapper). Echoes the old_string that was not found.

success.commentary: stdout is returned directly as the output content. No wrapping, no line numbers.

nonzero_exit.commentary: Nonzero exit returns an error (in the <error> wrapper) with just 'Exit code N'. No stdout content.

long_output.commentary: All 5000 lines returned without truncation. Bash output does NOT have a token cap like Read — full stdout is returned.

with_matches.commentary: Returns backslash-separated relative paths (on Windows), one per line, sorted by modification time (most recent first).

no_matches.commentary: Simple text message when no files match.

content_match.commentary: Content mode returns line_number:content format (colon-separated, no tab). Line numbers enabled by default.

content_no_match.commentary: Simple text message when no matches found.

files_with_matches.commentary: files_with_matches mode prefixes with 'Found N file(s)' then lists paths. Uses backslash paths on Windows.

single_select_answered.call: AskUserQuestion({questions: [{question: 'Which color do you prefer?', header: 'Test', options: [...], multiSelect: false}]})
single_select_answered.verbatim: Your questions have been answered: "This is a test question for tool output format capture. Which color do you prefer?"="Blue". You can now continue with these answers in mind.
single_select_answered.commentary: Returns a human-readable summary of answers in question=answer format. The full question text is echoed.

spawn_launch.call: Agent({description: 'Test agent spawn output', prompt: '...', subagent_type: 'claude'})
spawn_launch.verbatim:
Async agent launched successfully. (This tool result is internal metadata — never quote or paste any part of it, including the agentId below, into a user-facing reply.)
agentId: a8836098b05b518ef (internal ID - do not mention to user. Use SendMessage with to: 'a8836098b05b518ef', summary: '<5-10 word recap>' to continue this agent.)
The agent is working in the background. You will be notified automatically when it completes. You know nothing about its results until that notification arrives — do not report, assume, or predict them; continue other work or respond to the user in the meantime.
Do not duplicate this agent's work — avoid working with the same files or topics it is using.
output_file: C:\...\tasks\a8836098b05b518ef.output
Do NOT Read or tail this file via the shell tool — it is the full subagent JSONL transcript and reading it will overflow your context. If the user asks for progress, say the agent is still running; you'll get a completion notification.
spawn_launch.commentary: Agent launch is async. Tool result contains: agentId, instructions not to share it, SendMessage guidance, output_file path, and strong warnings not to read the output file or predict results.

completion_notification.call: (async notification — arrives as system-reminder in a subsequent turn, not as a direct tool result)
completion_notification.verbatim:
<task-notification>
<task-id>a8836098b05b518ef</task-id>
<tool-use-id>toolu_018hovTtcxa563tsYjrzeg1Z</tool-use-id>
<output-file>...tasks/a8836098b05b518ef.output</output-file>
<status>completed</status>
<summary>Agent "Test agent spawn output" finished</summary>
<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>AGENT_OUTPUT_CAPTURE_TEST_OK</result>
<usage><subagent_tokens>26770</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>0</tool_uses><duration_ms>2760</duration_ms></usage>

completion_notification.commentary: Completion arrives as a system-reminder containing a task-notification block. Includes: task-id, status, summary, the agent's final result text, and usage stats (tokens, tool uses, duration). Prefixed with a SYSTEM NOTIFICATION disclaimer warning this is not user input.

not_captured.commentary: Not exercised — no running background task available to stop without side effects. Would need a running agent or background bash task to capture.
